notes: The page is a blue typescript with dark handwritten corrections, numbered 74 above and archive 82 below. Its main text is cancelled by a single long diagonal. No title, date, signature, diagram or drawing was seen.

The first paragraph claims an equivalence between H-torsors and compatible torsor systems on the formal completion, and applies this to extensions. The second claims functoriality and compatibility with changes of complete traits. Section 7.6.3 discusses the corresponding adic-base setup and claims algebraizability by the method of 7.2 when S is normal. These are descriptions of document claims, not independently verified results.
The wording retained includes systêmes twice, cphérents, qutun, sbhéma local, and the repeated par un in schéma abélien par un [deleted schéma] tore. No grammatical repair was made.
The source calls algebraizability La question essentielle, but carries no explicit verification question or à vérifier note. The uncertainty marks in reading.tex are editorial.

H’s editorial description and its extended argument for reading the slashed oval as Z are not source ink and were not counted as ink discrepancies. The note-induced interruption before Appliquant is not used to infer an original paragraph break. An omitted extraction page macro is not treated as a discrepancy.

No mathematical completion determined a glyph. The possible identity of the group, the ring expected in an adic setup, and the role of the superscript round were not used to choose their forms. The symbol positions in Hom, the product, the tensor and the extension formulas were followed only to locate the ink for inspection.

Physical L1 begins ment; no preceding ellipsis is present. Ordinary line wrapping is joined. The section number is 7.6.3.; references are (7.6.1), 7.1 and 7.2, with no expansion. All three paragraph boundaries and the sheet cancellation are retained.

The short dark stroke below cancelled pe is reproduced spatially as an underline; its function (underlining, cancellation aid or line-end continuation mark) is not decided. The small q-shaped mark is likewise transcribed by shape without a linguistic interpretation.

The crowded blue raised mark above H is less decisive than the black circumflex above B. Its best reading is a circumflex, explicitly uncertain; its maker is unassigned. No alternative mathematical decoration with sufficient contour support was added.

All reported observations come from the assigned page. Whole and half images were each viewed once. Thirteen distinct tight crops were produced once each, autocontrasted and enlarged with LANCZOS, then viewed once in batches of at most three. No OCR, recognition, text extraction, external research, other-page inspection or reader comparison was performed.
